title: When the Orchard Turns
premise: In 1847, in the river town of Aldermoor, Felix Blackwood — a woman passing as a man to work as a mapmaker's apprentice — inherits her dead master's unfinished atlas of the contested orchard valley. When the seasonal bridge closes and a company militia arrives to erase the records of the tenant farmers' massacre, Felix must finish the atlas with the truth embedded in its margins before the victors' historians publish their sanitized version. Sheltered by the found family of surviving farmers and torn by love for the militia captain's sister, she smuggles the atlas out by river as the thaw comes, at the cost of her disguise, her safety, and nearly her life.
about_author: Bram Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed regional maps and land records. Their fiction draws on real cases where cartography became an act of quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unfinished Lines
chapters.summary: Felix Blackwood, disguised as a young man, works alone in her dead master's map room, tracing his final survey of the orchard valley. She finds a hidden annotation hinting the master died for what he mapped. POV: Felix. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Rope and River
chapters.summary: Felix travels to Aldermoor to interview farmers for the atlas's final plates. The ferryman warns that the bridge will close within days for the season. She meets Wren Calloway, a farmer's daughter who corrects her measurements with startling precision. POV: Felix. Beat: cautious connection.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren guides Felix through the orchards, pointing out scorch marks and unmarked graves the official record calls 'blight damage.' Felix realizes the master's annotations were testimony. POV: Felix. Beat: dawning horror beneath pastoral calm.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: On the bridge's final day, Felix hesitates between leaving and staying; a company rider seizes her master's preliminary sketches from a courier. She chooses to stay, sending only a decoy portfolio downstream. POV: Felix. Beat: the trap closes willingly.

chapters.title: A House Full of Strangers
chapters.summary: Snowbound in the Calloway farmhouse, Felix is folded into the family's rhythms — mending, arguing, singing off-key. For the first time since taking her brother's name, she feels seen without being known. POV: Felix. Beat: found family takes root.

chapters.title: The Captain's Sister
chapters.summary: Company militia arrives to 'survey for the new road.' Its cartographer is Edith Vane, Captain Vane's sister, who recognizes Felix's drafting hand instantly — and says nothing. POV: alternating Felix and Edith. Beat: recognition, threat, and unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: Two Maps, One Valley
chapters.summary: Edith and Felix are forced to collaborate on the company's official map. Each quietly drafts a different truth into the margins. They begin trading corrections like letters neither can send openly. POV: Edith. Beat: intimacy built from rivalry.

chapters.title: Testimony in Ink
chapters.summary: Old Tam Calloway agrees to dictate his account of the massacre night; Felix encodes it as contour lines and boundary notes only a trained eye could read. POV: Felix. Beat: fear transmuted into craft.

chapters.title: The Captain's Summons
chapters.summary: Captain Vane interrogates the household about 'seditious papers.' He reveals he knows a woman is hiding among them — he simply doesn't know which one. Wren covers for Felix instinctively. POV: Wren. Beat: loyalty tested under lamplight.

chapters.title: Thaw Water Rising
chapters.summary: An early thaw floods the low fields, destroying part of the master's original survey cache. Felix must redraw from memory while the river rises toward the mill where the farmers shelter. POV: Felix. Beat: nature tightening the clock.

chapters.title: Edith's Choice
chapters.summary: Edith discovers the encoded testimony in Felix's draft and confronts her privately. Instead of reporting it, she adds her own marginal note: her brother's written order for the massacre. POV: Edith. Beat: betrayal of blood for justice.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Mill
chapters.summary: Captain Vane, tipped off, orders the mill burned with the farmers' archive inside. The household saves what they can; Tam is badly injured shielding the testimony pages. POV: Wren. Beat: the cost becomes flesh and blood.

chapters.title: Night Surgery
chapters.summary: Felix tends Tam's burns through the night, and Wren discovers her secret — not the testimony, but the fact she is a woman. Wren keeps it, and something shifts between them. POV: Felix. Beat: vulnerability met with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Historian Arrives
chapters.summary: A company historian arrives to collect 'materials for the official record,' offering coin for any documents. The town's silence becomes its own quiet rebellion. POV: Edith. Beat: the race made explicit — ink against ink.

chapters.title: Margins and Confessions
chapters.summary: Felix and Edith finalize the true atlas: testimony, boundaries, grave sites, and the order itself, all hidden in plain sight. Edith confesses she once helped falsify a map and needs this to be her amends. POV: Edith. Beat: shared guilt, shared purpose.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren reveals she witnessed the massacre as a child and has never spoken of it; she dictates her account for the atlas. Her voice steadies instead of breaking. POV: Wren. Beat: testimony as reclamation.

chapters.title: The Search of the Map Room
chapters.summary: Vane raids the Calloway house and finds Felix's decoy portfolio — but also a slip proving Felix's identity. He arrests her as a spy and impostor, separating her from the finished atlas. POV: Felix. Beat: everything lost in one hour.

chapters.title: The Cell and the Key
chapters.summary: Imprisoned in the company storehouse, Felix bargains with a sympathetic guard using her drafting skill. Edith steals the atlas and the captain's order copy, choosing her brother's ruin over complicity. POV: Edith. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: River Ice Breaking
chapters.summary: Wren and the farmers stage a diversion at the broken bridge while Edith rows the atlas downriver through ice floes toward the capital's printing houses. Felix escapes in the chaos, wounded. POV: alternating. Beat: climax — every debt called at once.

chapters.title: The Reading Room
chapters.summary: Weeks later in the capital, a Royal Geographical Society clerk decodes the atlas margins; the massacre enters the public record hours before the company's version reaches print. Vane is recalled to face inquiry. POV: Edith. Beat: vindication, quiet and enormous.

chapters.title: When the Orchard Turns
chapters.summary: Spring returns to Aldermoor. Felix, no longer hiding, signs the completed atlas with her own name beside her master's. The farmers plant new trees over the old graves. POV: Felix. Beat: grief and love reconciled in open light.

chapters.title: Appendix: A Cartographer's Note
chapters.summary: An epilogue framed as Felix's published preface to the atlas, addressing future readers: maps are promises about what is real, and someone must keep drawing the truth. She names Wren, Edith, and Tam in print. POV: Felix. Beat: legacy sealed, story complete.
